questions.question: What is an indicator of self-reliance?

options.text: Increase in imports of the goods which could be produced in the country.
Avoiding imports of the goods which could be produced in the country.
Increase in exports of the goods which could not be produced in the country.
Avoiding exports of the goods which could be produced in the country.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Avoiding imports of the goods which could be produced in the country**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A self-reliant economy is one that does not require any aid, support, interaction or trade with the outside world**.
 
• Avoiding imports of the goods which could be produced in the country will utilise the available resources within the country and will lower the burden to borrow from outside the country. **Hence it is an indicator of being self-reliant**.
 
• An increase in imports of the goods which could be produced in the country will increase the burden of the country to borrow from other countries. **Hence it is not an indicator of Self-reliance**.
 
• An increase in exports of goods which could not be produced in the country will create an extra burden on the economy of the country.** Hence it is not an indicator of Self - reliance**.
 
• Avoiding exports of the goods which could be produced in the country will lose the chance of strengthening the economy of the country. **Hence it is not an indicator of Self - reliance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan (meaning self-reliant India scheme) was announced in four tranches by the Union Finance Minister** Nirmala Sitharaman in May 2020**.
 
• The Prime Minister announced that an Atmanirbhar Bharat or a self-reliant India should stand on the following five pillars
 
 
• Economy
 
• Infrastructure
 
• 21st-century technology-driven arrangements and system
 
• Demand
 
• Vibrant Demography

questions.question: When a person is NOT paying anything for public goods, it is known as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**free rider**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A free rider is a person who benefits from resources, goods, or services without paying for the cost of the benefit.
 
• This phenomenon commonly occurs with public goods, which are non-excludable and non-rivalrous.
 
• Free rider problem can lead to under-provision of public goods as there is no incentive for individuals to contribute voluntarily.
 
• Government intervention is often required to ensure the provision and maintenance of public goods due to the free rider problem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-excludable:**

 
 
• Non-excludable goods are those that individuals cannot be effectively excluded from using.
 
• Examples include public parks, national defense, and clean air.
 
 
 
• **Rivalrous:**
 
 
• Rivalrous goods are those that can only be used by one person at a time.
 
• If one person consumes a rivalrous good, it reduces the amount available for others.
 
• Examples include food, clothing, and cars.
 
 
 
• **Private good:**
 
 
• Private goods are both excludable and rivalrous.
 
• Owners can prevent others from using them, and their use by one person diminishes their availability to others.
 
• Examples include personal electronics, houses, and personal vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Free rider problem:**
 
 
• This occurs when individuals benefit from resources, goods, or services without paying for them.
 
• It is particularly prevalent with public goods which are non-excludable and non-rivalrous.
 
• Common solutions involve government intervention or collective action to provide the good and ensure everyone contributes.

questions.question: Government goods and services that aren't sold directly to the consumers, for example defence goods, roads are categorised under:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** public goods.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Public Good:

 
 
• Public goods are goods that are commonly available to all people within a society or community and that possess two specific qualities: they are non-excludable and non-rivalrous. Everyone has access to use them, and their use does not deplete their availability for future use.
 
• A commodity whose benefits are indivisibly spread among the entire community.
 
• Non-excludability - Individuals or groups of individuals can’t be specifically excluded from using the goods
 
• Non-rivalry - The use of the goods by some individuals doesn’t cause a reduction in their availability to others, which would thereby violate the first quality
 
• Public goods are generally considered goods that are available to anyone.
 
• They differ from common goods in that the latter are typically non-excludable but are usually rivalrous to some extent.
 
• Wild game used for food is an example of a common good.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• 
 
 
• People cannot generally be excluded from obtaining and using it; however, the same animals cannot be used more than once.
 
• The list of public goods varies, depending on how specifically the term is viewed. However, common examples of public goods include:
 
• Street lighting - It is generally provided by communities and consumption/use of the lighting doesn’t prevent others from using it as well.
 
• Emergency services - They are provided to communities, and their use benefits and strengthens the community.
 
• National defense - Whether paid or voluntary, national defense services protect the country as a whole.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a monopoly?

options.text: Full control over the price by the seller

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One buyer and many sellers**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A monopoly is characterized by **one seller and many buyers**.
 
• In a monopoly, there are **no close substitutes** for the product or service provided by the seller.
 
• The seller in a monopoly has **full control over the price** of the product or service.
 
• The market condition of **one buyer and many sellers** describes a monopsony, not a monopoly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **monopoly** exists when a specific person or enterprise is the only supplier of a particular commodity.
 
• This contrasts with a **monopsony** where there is only one buyer and many sellers.
 
• Monopolies can be established by a government, form naturally over time, or form as a conglomerate of companies.
 
• Monopolies can lead to **higher prices and inferior products** due to the lack of competition.
 
• Antitrust laws in many countries regulate monopolistic practices to protect consumers.

questions.question: When exports are higher than imports, it is known as a situation of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** trade surplus.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Trade Surplus:- **

 
 
• A trade surplus occurs when a country sells more goods and services to other countries than it buys from them.
 
• This means that money is flowing into the country from abroad.
 
• When exports are higher than imports, it is also known as a situation of Trade Surplus 
 
• A trade surplus can have a number of positive effects on an economy, such as boosting economic growth, creating jobs, and increasing the value of the country's currency.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trade Deficit:- **

 
 
• A trade deficit occurs when a country imports more goods and services than it exports.
 
• It is calculated by subtracting the value of a country's exports from the value of its imports.
 
• A trade deficit can be a sign of a strong economy, as it indicates that consumers have sufficient resources to purchase more goods than are produced domestically. 
 
 
 
• ** Fiscal Deficit:-**
 
 
• A fiscal deficit occurs when a government spends more money than it collects in revenue.
 
• It is calculated by subtracting total government revenue from total government expenditure.
 
• A fiscal deficit can be financed by borrowing money from domestic or foreign sources, or by printing money.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Surplus:-**
 
 
• A revenue surplus occurs when a government collects more revenue than it spends.
 
• It is calculated by subtracting total government expenditure from total government revenue.
 
• A revenue surplus can be used to pay down debt, invest in public goods and services, or provide tax cuts.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the demand curve?

I. It is a graphical representation of the demand function.

II. It gives the quantity demanded by the consumer at each price.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A demand curve is a graphical representation of the demand function.**
 
• It shows the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity demanded by consumers.
 
• The demand curve slopes downward from left to right, which means that as the price of a good decrease, the quantity demanded increases.
 
• This is because consumers are willing and able to buy more of a good at a lower price.
 
• **The demand curve also gives the quantity demanded by the consumer at each price.**
 
• For example, if the price of a good is ₹10, the consumer is willing and able to buy 10 units of the good.
 
• If the price of the good decreases to ₹5, the consumer is willing and able to buy 20 units of the good.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Demand Curve and the Law of Demand

 
 
• ​If the prices of other goods, the consumer’s income and her tastes and preferences remain unchanged, the amount of a good that the consumer optimally chooses becomes entirely dependent on its price.
 
• The relation between the consumer’s optimal choice of the quantity of a good and its price is very important and this relation is called the demand function.
 
• Factors that affect the demand curve:
 
 
• ​Income
 
• Changing Tastes or Preferences
 
• Changes in the Composition of the Population
 
 
 
• Demand Curve 
 
 
• The demand curve is a relation between the quantity of the good chosen by a consumer and the price of the good.
 
• The** independent variable (price) is measured along the vertical axis and the dependent variable (quantity) is measured along the horizontal axis.**
 
• The demand curve gives the quantity demanded by the consumer at each price.

questions.question:
What happens in case of market equilibrium:

(a) Market demand = market supply

(b) There is no excess supply in the market
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (a) and (b).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The market attains equilibrium when the market supply and market demand of a commodity become equal.
 
• The term supply refers to how much of a certain product, item, commodity, or service suppliers are willing to make available at a particular price
 
• Demand refers to how much of that product, item, commodity, or service consumers are willing and able to purchase at a particular price
 
• Supply and demand are economic forces of the free market that control what suppliers are willing to produce and what consumers are willing and able to purchase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If the market price is above the equilibrium value, there is an excess supply in the market (a surplus), which means there is more supply than demand.
 
• If the market price is below the equilibrium value, then there is an excess in demand (supply shortage).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9042c9dca25efe9625d51e525814238bd7e86f2da7945bd56a70fc82bed307ae.png]

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of the six communication mail channels in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monthly channel**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The six communication mail channels in India are crucial for the efficient delivery of mail across the country.
 
• These channels include the **Metro channel, Rajdhani channel, Business channel, Bulk mail channel, Periodical channel,** and the **Express channel**.
 
• The **Monthly channel** is not a recognized communication mail channel in India.
 
• Each of these channels is designed to cater to specific types of mail and delivery requirements, ensuring timely and organized mail distribution.
 
• The **Metro channel** focuses on mail within metropolitan areas, while the **Rajdhani channel** is for express mail between major cities.
 
• The **Business channel** and **Bulk mail channel** handle large volumes of business and bulk mail, respectively.
 
• The **Periodical channel** is dedicated to the distribution of periodicals and magazines, and the **Express channel** is used for urgent deliveries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indian postal system **is one of the most extensive networks in the world, playing a vital role in communication and logistics.
 
• Established in **1854**, the Indian postal service has evolved significantly, adapting to modern communication needs while maintaining traditional services.
 
• The postal system also supports various financial services, including savings accounts, insurance, and money transfer services.
 
• With the advent of digital communication, the Indian postal service has integrated technology to enhance efficiency and service delivery.
 
• Initiatives such as e-post, track and trace, and online postal services have modernized the traditional postal system, making it more accessible and user-friendly.

questions.question: Addition to the stock of capital of a firm is known as __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Investment**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The addition to a firm's capital stock is known as an investment.
 
• Investment is the process of purchasing assets to generate income or appreciation in the future.
 
• It can also be referred to as capital formation. 
 
• Investment is a broader concept than capital formation, which is the accounting value of new non-financial assets added to the capital stock.
 
• Investment can include all types of capital assets, such as physical property or financial assets. 
 
• Investing is the act of allocating resources, usually capital, with the expectation of generating an income, profit, or gains. Investors typically consider that a greater period of time, like months or years, is needed to generate acceptable returns. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Accumulation
 
 
• Accumulation refers to the process of gathering or increasing resources, assets, or wealth over time. It can apply to financial savings, investments, or even physical goods.
 
• In Economics: It is often associated with the gradual build-up of capital or wealth through saving and reinvesting profits.
 
• Example: A person saving money in a bank account over several years is an example of wealth accumulation.
 
 
 
• Capital Loss
 
 
• A capital loss occurs when the value of an asset decreases, and it is sold for less than its original purchase price.
 
• In Economics/Finance: It is the opposite of a capital gain and often impacts a firm's or individual's financial health negatively.
 
• Example: Selling a property for ₹8 lakh when it was purchased for ₹10 lakh results in a ₹2 lakh capital loss.
 
 
 
• Capital Gain
 
 
• A capital gain occurs when an asset increases in value and is sold for more than its original purchase price.
 
• In Economics/Finance: Capital gains are often taxable and are a common source of income for investors.
 
• Example: Selling stocks for ₹5 lakh that were purchased for ₹3 lakh results in a ₹2 lakh capital gain.

questions.question: Which of the following goods needs further transformation in the economic process?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Intermediate goods**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Intermediate goods need further transformation in the economic process:
 
• Intermediate goods:
 
 
• These are partially finished goods that are used to make other goods.
 
 
 
• They are also known as producer goods.
 
• Intermediate goods undergo further processing and transformation to become final goods.
 
• For example, a car component can be an intermediate good if it is incorporated into a vehicle, or a final good if it is sold to the consumer as a spare part.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Consumer durable goods
 
 
• A type of consumer good that lasts for more than three years and is purchased infrequently.
 
• Examples include appliances, cars, and furniture. 
 
 
 
• Finished goods
 
 
• A finished product that is purchased by consumers for personal or household use.
 
• Examples include food, clothing, vehicles, electronics, and appliances. 
 
 
 
• Capital goods
 
 
• A tangible product that is used to produce goods and services, and is not typically sold to consumers.
 
• Examples include buildings, machinery, vehicles, large tools, and equipment

questions.question:
Consider the following methods adopted by the government to protect goods produced in India from imports.

(i) Heavy taxes were levied on imported goods

(ii) The maximum limit on the imports of a commodity by a domestic user was fixed Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Both (i) and (ii) are true**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Heavy taxes** on imported goods are commonly used by governments to protect domestic industries by making imported goods more expensive, thereby encouraging consumers to buy locally produced goods.
 
• **Import limits**, or quotas, are another method used to restrict the quantity of a specific commodity that can be imported, ensuring that domestic producers have a significant share of the market.
 
• Both of these measures are part of a broader strategy known as **protectionism**, aimed at safeguarding national economic interests.
 
• Protectionist policies are often adopted to help nascent industries develop without the pressure of international competition.
 
• These measures can help in boosting the local economy, increasing employment, and fostering the growth of domestic industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tariffs:**

 
 
• Tariffs are taxes imposed by a government on goods and services imported from other countries, making them more expensive and less attractive compared to domestic products.
 
• They are used to restrict imports, raise government revenue, or protect domestic industries from foreign competition.
 
 
 
• **Quotas:**
 
 
• Quotas are limits set by a government on the amount of a specific product that can be imported over a set period of time.
 
• This method directly restricts the quantity of goods entering a country, thereby protecting domestic industries from excessive foreign competition.
 
 
 
• **Subsidies:**
 
 
• Subsidies are financial aids provided by the government to domestic industries to lower their production costs and make their products more competitive against imported goods.
 
• They can take various forms, such as direct cash payments, tax breaks, or low-interest loans.
 
 
 
• **Non-Tariff Barriers (NTBs):**
 
 
• NTBs include various regulations and standards imposed by a country to restrict imports without using tariffs, such as stringent quality standards, licensing requirements, and customs procedures.
 
• These barriers can significantly impact the volume of imports and protect domestic industries.

questions.question: _______________ is an indicator used by experts to gauge the number of people dying prematurely due to a particular disease
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**global burden of diseases.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Global Burden of Disease:-**

 
 
• GBD is the sum of all health loss from diseases, injuries, and risk factors across a population.
 
• **It is measured in disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), which are a unit that combines years of life lost to premature death with years lived in disability.**
 
• The GBD study is the most comprehensive and widely used measure of global health.
 
• **It is conducted by the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) at the University of Washington, and it is published annually in the Lancet medical journal.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Domestic Diseases:-**

 
 
• **GDD is a satirical term used to describe the negative consequences of economic growth, such as environmental degradation, income inequality, and social alienation. **
 
• It is a play on the term "gross domestic product" (GDP), which is a measure of the total value of all goods and services produced in a country within a given period of time.
 
 
 
• **Goods and services tax:-**
 
 
• **GST is a value-added tax (VAT) that is levied on most goods and services sold for domestic consumption. **
 
• The GST is paid by consumers, but it is remitted to the government by the businesses selling the goods and services.
 
 
 
• **Gross national product:-**
 
 
• **GNP is the total market value of all final goods and services produced by a nation's economy during a specific period of time (usually a year),** computed before allowance is made for the depreciation or consumption of capital used in the process of production.

questions.question: The number of deaths during the first 28 completed days of life per 1000 live births in a given year or period is defined as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**neonatal mortality rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The number of deaths during the first 28 completed days of life per 1000 live births** in a given year or period is defined as **the neonatal mortality rate**.
 
• There are some concerns about the quality of neonatal mortality reporting both internationally and within states, particularly in terms of defining a live birth and/or reporting both birth and death certificates for newborns with very low birth weights.
 
• When neonatal death certificates are matched to corresponding birth certificates, much more additional and valuable data (birth weight, mother's smoking status, when prenatal care began, etc.) is obtained for neonatal mortality risk analysis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The number of newborn deaths per 1,000 live births is known as t**he infant mortality rate. **
 
• **The infant mortality rate** is an essential indicator of a society's general health, in addition to providing crucial information regarding maternal and baby health.
 
• **The crude mortality rate **is derived by dividing the number of fatalities in a particular time by the number of people who were at risk of dying during that period.
 
• A death rate that is limited to a certain age group is known as an **age-specific mortality rate.**

questions.question: According to __________ policy, instead of importing vehicles made in a foreign country, industries would be encouraged to produce them in India itself.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Import substitution**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the import substitution policy, instead of importing vehicles made in a foreign country, industries are encouraged to produce them domestically in India to reduce dependency on foreign goods and promote local manufacturing.
 
• Import substitution is an economic policy that focuses on reducing reliance on foreign imports by promoting domestic production of goods and services. 
 
• The idea is to encourage industries within the country to manufacture products that would otherwise be imported, thereby fostering self-reliance and reducing the trade deficit.
 
• Example in India:
 
• Automobile Sector:
 
• During the 1950s and 1960s, India adopted the policy of import substitution under its five-year plans. The government restricted the import of automobiles and encouraged domestic companies like Tata Motors and Hindustan Motors to produce vehicles locally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indian substitution
 
 
• This term does not exist as an economic policy. It seems fabricated or irrelevant in the context of economic frameworks.
 
• There's no policy specifically named "Indian substitution."
 
 
 
• Export substitution
 
 
• This refers to policies or strategies that encourage producing goods primarily for export rather than for domestic consumption.
 
• The focus of export substitution is on earning foreign exchange by exporting goods rather than importing them, which is opposite to what is described in the question.
 
 
 
• Ruralisation
 
 
• This refers to policies aimed at promoting rural development or prioritizing the rural economy.
 
• It generally involves encouraging agriculture, rural industries, and decentralized development rather than focusing on industrial production like vehicles.

questions.question: The production function can be expressed as _______. (where L is labour and C is capital and Q is the maximum output that can be produced)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Q = f(L, C)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The production function is a mathematical** representation of the relationship between inputs (like labour and capital) and the output of a firm or industry.**
 
• The production function typically takes the form
 
 
• **Q = f(L, C)**
 
• **Where Q represents the maximum output that can be produced given the inputs.**

questions.question: If ex ante aggregate demand and ex ante aggregate supply are plotted together in a graphical diagram, then at which point equilibrium will be reached?

options.text: Where ex ante aggregate demand is less than ex ante aggregate supply
Where ex ante aggregate demand is equal to ex ante aggregate supply
Where ex ante aggregate demand is more than ex ante aggregate supply
Where ex ante aggregate demand is zero

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__**.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** In a graphical diagram where ex ante aggregate demand (AD) and ex ante aggregate supply (AS) are plotted together, equilibrium is reached at the point where the two curves intersect.**
 
• This intersection represents the level of real output and price level where** the quantity of goods and services demanded (AD) is equal to the quantity supplied (AS).**
 
• **At this equilibrium point**, there is no tendency for the economy to move away from it, as the quantity demanded matches the quantity supplied.
 
• **The equilibrium point** can be thought of as the point of balance in the economy, where there is no excess demand or excess supply.
 
• It is where **buyers' and sellers' **plans align, resulting in a stable state in which the economy is in equilibrium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **In an economy, demand and supply refer to the forces that determine the quantity** **of goods and services exchanged in the market. **

 
 
• **Demand: **Demand represents the quantity of goods and services that buyers are willing and able to purchase at various price levels, during a specific period.

 
 
• Demand is influenced by factors such as price, consumer preferences, income levels, population, and the availability of substitutes.
 
• The relationship between price and quantity demanded is typically inverse, meaning that as the price increases, the quantity demanded tends to decrease, and vice versa.
 
• Demand is usually represented by a downward-sloping demand curve.
 
 
 
• **Supply: **Supply, on the other hand, represents the quantity of goods and services that sellers are willing and able to offer for sale at different price levels.
 
 
• The supply is influenced by factors such as production costs, technology, resource availability, government regulations, and expectations of future prices.
 
• The relationship between price and quantity supplied is usually positive, meaning that as the price increases, the quantity supplied tends to increase, and vice versa.
 
• Supply is often represented by an upward-sloping supply curve.
 
 
 
• **The interaction of demand and supply determines** **the equilibrium price** **and quantity in a market.**
 
 
• When the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied, the market is said to be in equilibrium.
 
• Changes in demand or supply will shift the respective curves, leading to changes in the equilibrium price and quantity.
 
• For example, an increase in demand will shift the demand curve to the right, leading to a higher equilibrium price and quantity.
 
 
 
 
 
• Understanding the dynamics of demand and supply is crucial in analyzing market behavior, price fluctuations, and the allocation of resources in an economy.

Public goods possess which of the following features in the economy?

II. They are non-excludable.

__
 
• Public goods are goods or services that are consumed by everyone in the society, regardless of whether they have paid for it or not.
 
• **Non-rivalrous means that one person's consumption of the good does not reduce the amount available for others.**
 
• For example, if a park is a **public good,** one person's enjoyment of the park does not prevent others from enjoying it as well.
 
• **Non-excludable means that it is difficult or impossible to prevent someone from consuming the good, even if they have not paid for it.**
 
• For example, it is difficult to prevent someone from enjoying the view of a fireworks display from a public space, even if they have not paid for a ticket to attend the event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Private goods are goods or services that are consumed by individuals who have paid for them.
 
• **Private goods** **are both** **rivalrous and excludable.**
 
• **Common goods are goods or services that are available to everyone in the society but are rivalrous.**
 
• For example,** fish in a lake **can be a common good because if one person catches a fish, there is one less fish available for others to catch.
 
• **Club goods are goods or services that are non-rivalrous but excludable.**
 
• For example, a subscription to a streaming service is a club good because multiple people can consume the service at the same time without reducing the amount available for others, but only those who have paid for the subscription can access it.

questions.question: The country can improve its balance of payments by devaluation when the sum of elasticity of demand for exports and imports is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**greater than unity.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Devaluation** is the **reduction** in the value of a **country's currency relative** to other currencies.
 
• The** elasticity of demand** refers to the responsiveness of** demand for a good or service** to a change in its price.
 
• When the** sum of elasticity **of demand for** exports and imports **is **greater than unity,** a** devaluation** can improve the balance of payments.
 
• This is because a devaluation makes **exports cheaper and imports more expensive**, which can increase the** demand for exports** and **reduce the demand for imports**, thereby** improving the balance of payments**.
 
• When the** sum of elasticity** of demand for **exports and imports **is less than **unity or equal to unity**, devaluation may not be effective in** improving the balance of payments.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If the sum of elasticity of demand for exports and imports is **less than unity**, devaluation may not lead to a significant increase in demand for exports or decrease in demand for imports.
 
• If the sum of elasticity of demand for exports and imports is** equal to unity,** devaluation may lead to a proportionate increase in demand for exports and decrease in demand for imports, but may not necessarily improve the balance of payments. 
 
• If the sum of elasticity of demand for exports and imports is** zero**, devaluation will not have any effect on the demand for exports or imports, and hence will not improve the balance of payments.

questions.question:
In which of the following ways, aggregate demand function is related to consumption function?

I. They have the same slope C.

II. The aggregate demand function is parallel to the consumption function.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The slope of the consumption function represents the marginal propensity to consume (MPC), which is the change in consumption resulting from a change in income.
 
• The aggregate demand function also includes consumption as a component, and therefore, the slope of the aggregate demand function is determined by the marginal propensity to consume. So, they have the same slope.
 
• The aggregate demand function consists of several components, including consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports.
 
• While the consumption function represents the relationship between consumption and income, the aggregate demand function represents the relationship between aggregate demand (total spending) and the overall price level.
 
• The aggregate demand function can be considered as the sum of all spending components, including consumption. Since consumption is a part of aggregate demand, the aggregate demand function and the consumption function are parallel to each other.

Therefore, both statements I and II are correct.

• **Currencies **from most **developing countries **are **considered **to be** soft currencies**.

• **Marginal cost: **It is additional cost of producing one more unit of output.
